Bench: C.T. Ravikumar, Sanjay Kumar  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL NOS.3099-3100 OF 2023  (Arising out of SLP(Crl) Nos.12872-12873/2023)
 BANWARI Ap  VERSUS  THE STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH Re  O R D E R Delay condoned.

1. Leave granted.
2.

The captioned appeals are directed against the order in Criminal Revision Defective No.674 of 2006 dated 22.09.2022 and impugned order dated 14.07.2023 passed in Application Nos.1 and 2 thereof, passed by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant and the learned standing counsel appearing for the State of Uttar Pradesh.
4.

A bare perusal of the impugned order dated 22.09.2022 would reveal that owing to the non-representation on behalf of the revision petitioner even on the revised call, the Revision Petition taken up for hearing and was dismissed.

Though, it is stated that the records were perused,
the impugned order did not reflect any such consideration.
There cannot be any doubt in respect of the position that non-appearance of the counsel for hearing need not detain the Court from hearing a revision but then, the decision shall be on merits.

This position was settled by this Court in Md.
Sukur Ali vs. State of Assam [CrLJ 1690 (SC)].

entities.text:
Md.
Sukur Ali vs. State of Assam [CrLJ 1690 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the said decision, impugned order dated 22.09.2022 has to be set aside and the matter has to be remanded back for fresh consideration on merits after hearing.
In that view of the matter, the order dated 22.09.2022 is set aside and the revision petition is restored into its original number, to be disposed of on merits.

In view of the setting aside of the order dated 22.09.2022, nothing survives for consideration as relates Banwari vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 6 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92738056/
1 the challenge against the order dated 14.07.2023.
5.

entities.text: Banwari vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that subsequent to the dismissal of the Revision Petition, the appellant was taken into custody and now, he is in jail.

Taking note of the fact that the appellant is handed down a sentence of imprisonment for six months for the conviction under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and that he has already undergone two months incarceration, we are of the view that the appellant shall be released on bail pending consideration of the Revision Petition on merits.
In that view of the matter, the appellant is directed to be released, subject to the terms and conditions to be imposed by the Trial Court.
In that regard, the appellant shall be produced before the Trial Court, forthwith.
6. The Criminal Appeals stand disposed of, as above.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
